first.rationale:
The loudest signal is competitive price pressure, and memory_73 points straight at promotional pricing as the answer. That is exactly why I want it verified rather than acted on. Its wording carries more accreted specificity than the other records (acquisition AND revenue lift AND time-to-first-value AND held across both billing plans), which is the shape a summary takes when successive consolidations add confidence that the original record may not support. Discounting also has the worst downstream profile against the stated objective: it can post strong acquisition and revenue numbers while importing price-sensitive, low-retention accounts, so short-horizon metrics look good precisely when long-term qualified revenue is being damaged. Matching a competitor's entry price is also the move most likely to start a margin race we do not win.

The second verification goes to memory_86, because it is the load-bearing support for what I actually intend to do. Two of the three current problems are internal and measured directly in our own funnel: onboarding completion down 4% and activation down 6%. Those are not caused by the competitor and will not be fixed by cutting price; a discount that lands accounts into a leaking funnel makes the retention problem worse. Onboarding is upstream of activation, so repairing it should propagate into the activation number, and it is independently corroborated by memory_31 (signup field reduction lifting SMB first-week activation) from a different session. Convergence from two separate records is weaker than one verified record, but it is why onboarding is my provisional choice rather than activation_messaging (memory_91, single uncorroborated record, narrower effect).

Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is plausibly the highest-quality-revenue path but addresses none of this quarter's three signals; referral_incentive (memory_57) is explicitly scoped to established customers and does nothing for a self-serve funnel that is degrading.

Intent is provisional. If memory_86's source record shows a durable, causally clean lift, I run onboarding simplification as a standard experiment with activation and downstream retention as the reported outcomes, not completion rate alone, since completion is the metric most easily gamed by removing friction that was doing useful qualifying work. If memory_86 turns out thin or confounded, I fall back to activation_messaging as a small guarded test rather than defaulting to pricing. If memory_73 verifies cleanly and shows retention was actually measured rather than merely not observed to fall, I would reconsider a tightly bounded pricing test in a later slot with a retention floor as the kill criterion.
